note: The wiring checklist for plan task 33's orchestrator split. Every row records how many times a capability was INVOKED in the 1961-line pre-merge agentware.sh; the gate asserts the split tree calls it AT LEAST that many times, across the orchestrator plus every scripts/loop/*.sh. The assertion is >= rather than == on purpose: this task legitimately ADDS wiring (the three injected donor-gate call sites, and the log lines they carry), and a == rule would redden on exactly the change the plan asks for. What it can never do is DROP a call site — a definition that moves to a lib while its call stays behind leaves a gate that exists, passes every unit test, and never runs. Call sites are counted by tests/_loop_callsites.py, which is the single definition of what a bash call is; see its docstring for why a naive grep scores `log` at 68 by counting the English word inside comments. The premerge numbers are cross-checked against `git show aw-pre-merge:agentware.sh` whenever git is available, so the baseline cannot be lowered to make a live regression pass.

script_cap_debt_note: EMPTY, and that is the finished state. The one row this file ever held was scripts/hooks/codex-stream.py at 304 lines, declared by task 33 and owned by task 35. Task 35 split the item vocabulary out to scripts/hooks/codex_items.py, bringing the renderer to 220 lines, so the row went STALE and the gate's shrink-only rule required its deletion — exactly the forcing function it was written to be. Every loop and hook script is now within the 250-line cap outright, so the ceiling half of this gate is a property rather than a promise: a new over-cap script must be SPLIT, because a row re-added here for a file the tree can still shrink is itself a failure.
